strengths: Strong theoretical foundation with rigorous proofs connecting stochastic flow maps to value function estimation
Novel application of flow maps to reward alignment with creative 'Diamond Maps' framework featuring inner/outer time structure
Demonstrates practical efficiency gains enabling one-step 'look-ahead' sampling while maintaining value function accuracy
Solid empirical validation on benchmark tasks with consistent improvements over baselines in guidance quality and robustness
Comprehensive treatment with two practical variants and clear algorithm descriptions
Addresses real problem in generative modeling where existing approaches have clear tradeoffs
Well-organized presentation with clear motivation and detailed mathematical appendix
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope with only two datasets (CIFAR-10, CelebA) and relatively small models due to compute constraints
Incremental novelty building heavily on recent GLASS flow and flow matching work rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts
Modest practical improvements in some cases (~3-5% absolute gains over Best-of-N in certain metrics)
Optimistic assumptions about GLASS flow distillation quality without thorough error analysis or failure mode discussion
Key experimental details and hyperparameter justifications relegated to appendix, limiting evaluability in main text
Limited wall-clock time comparisons and computational cost analysis versus baselines
Incomplete ablation studies on design choices such as time-reparameterization optimality and hyperparameter sensitivity
No clear guidance on when to prefer Posterior versus Weighted Diamond Map variant in practice

strengths: Technically sound with formal proofs establishing consistency and efficiency of the proposed estimators (Propositions 4.1, 4.3, 5.1)
Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple domains (image generation, text-to-image, super-resolution) with consistent improvements over strong baselines
Novel and clever use of flow maps for efficient value function estimation, with thoughtful design choices (reparameterization, renoising procedure)
Clear problem motivation addressing the important challenge of efficient reward alignment in diffusion/flow models
Practical method demonstrating efficiency gains and enabling scalable guidance with reduced computational cost
Thorough experimental reporting with quantitative metrics (FID, LPIPS, KID) and qualitative results across diverse settings
Honest and transparent discussion of limitations and assumptions in Section 8
weaknesses: Somewhat incremental contribution that primarily combines recently published techniques (GLASS Flows, flow maps, value function estimation) rather than introducing fundamentally novel concepts
Method's applicability fundamentally limited by dependence on pre-trained flow models, which may not exist for all domains of interest
Improvements over baselines are sometimes modest (e.g., Tables 3-4, Figures 8-9), raising questions about practical significance in certain settings
Limited theoretical analysis of robustness: no convergence rates, finite-sample error bounds, or analysis of sensitivity to imperfect flow maps provided
Dense presentation (36 pages) with complex algorithms that could be explained more intuitively; important details relegated to appendix
Computational requirements remain substantial (8x L40S GPUs) despite efficiency claims, potentially limiting accessibility
Missing ablation studies on some key design choices (e.g., specific form of GLASS velocity field distillation, importance of recovery reward formulation)
